programs.title: Foundations
programs.historicalNote: Identified as a recorded RSD program by April 2007 (R01).
programs.cardHeadline: Before the advanced stuff, master the basics.
programs.shortCopy: Foundations takes you back to the practical side of early RSD: meeting people, starting interactions, and navigating social situations and logistics. It sits at the beginning of the archive's story, before the instructor-specific collections and the later personal-development releases.
programs.expandedCopy: If you arrived through a later personal-growth program, this is a place to study the earlier teaching context. Approach it as a historical starting point, then compare its practical emphasis with other programs instead of expecting one recording to answer every social question.
programs.audienceFit: Customers seeking the earliest chapters rather than another recent personal-growth course.
programs.publicNotes: Exact included edition to be confirmed.

programs.title: Transformations
programs.instructor: Multi-instructor RSD, with special guests Ozzie & Hoobie
programs.historicalNote: Identified as a recorded multi-instructor RSD program by April 2007 (R01).
programs.cardHeadline: One problem. Multiple instructors. Completely different answers.
programs.shortCopy: See how different early RSD instructors approached confidence, social skills, and inner game from their own perspectives, including special guest instructors Ozzie and Hoobie. It shows RSD as a company of voices rather than a single personality.
programs.expandedCopy: Study how different presenters framed similar social questions, from the core RSD instructors to special guests Ozzie and Hoobie. For a returning personal-growth customer, the value is context: different styles, different explanations, and a clearer sense of the broader library. This is the original multi-instructor Transformations, not Julien's later transformation work.
verifiedThemes: Special guest instructors Ozzie and Hoobie
programs.audienceFit: Customers interested in comparing perspectives.
programs.publicNotes: Distinct from Julien's later transformation work.
programs.guestSourceNote: Owner-stated (2026-10-01). Confirm against the Transformations edition files and credit spellings before launch.

programs.title: The Blueprint Decoded
programs.historicalNote: Multi-day original presentation discussed on the RSD blog in 2007–2008 (R01, R02).
programs.cardHeadline: What if the "techniques" were never the real point?
programs.shortCopy: The Blueprint Decoded is Tyler's extended RSD presentation about the larger ideas behind social interaction. Its historical framing emphasizes a connected body of teaching rather than isolated lines or tips.
programs.expandedCopy: Make this a comparison point in your prequel journey. Study the instructor's explanations, identify the assumptions behind them, and decide what deserves testing in your own experience. The archive preserves the presentation as historical teaching, not as a new scientific model or a guarantee of personal transformation.
programs.audienceFit: Learners who prefer conceptual context alongside practical material.
programs.publicNotes: Running time, disc count and topics only after edition inspection.

programs.title: Hot Seat at Home
programs.cardHeadline: Study interactions with the benefit of a pause button.
programs.shortCopy: Historical Hot Seat at Home listings describe interaction footage, breakdowns, and exercises. It is intended as an observation-based counterpart to presentation-led courses.
programs.expandedCopy: Use the included, verified examples to consider what was said, how it was delivered, and how another person responded. Pause, take notes, and discuss your interpretation with your coach. The included edition determines which recordings and exercises you receive; an old Mastermind upgrade is not automatically an additional standalone program.
programs.audienceFit: Viewers who learn through examples.
programs.publicNotes: Identifiable people in footage require distribution review.

programs.title: PIMP
programs.cardHeadline: Before Julien's later transformation work, there was an earlier chapter.
programs.shortCopy: PIMP is a separate legacy program from SHIFT and TenGame. For customers who know Julien through later personal-growth work, it supplies an earlier dating-focused point of reference within the archive.
programs.expandedCopy: The reason to include this in your study path is historical perspective: compare an earlier approach with what you have already learned, rather than assume the programs teach identical ideas. Inspect the exact edition and contents before purchasing. PIMP is presented as an archival release, not as a new Julien program or a promise of his current involvement.
programs.audienceFit: Julien-aware customers seeking the earlier material they do not already own.
programs.publicNotes: No texting, mentoring, hours, modules or tier names until verified. Never 'Pimp Shift'.

programs.title: SHIFT (Making a SHIFT)
programs.cardHeadline: Study the relationship between identity and experience.
programs.shortCopy: SHIFT's historical positioning addresses beliefs, motivation, validation, identity, growth, and momentum in social and dating situations. It is a separate program from PIMP.
programs.expandedCopy: If personal growth is familiar territory, this is an earlier point of comparison: how did the instructor connect what a person believed about themselves with what they did in the social world? Study the framework critically and compare it with the later material. Exact chapters, examples, and bonuses depend on the released edition.
programs.audienceFit: Customers interested in the bridge between self-concept and action.
programs.publicNotes: Separate from PIMP.

programs.title: TenGame (The Ten Game)
programs.cardHeadline: Principles to study. Practice to reflect on.
programs.shortCopy: Historical TenGame inventories describe a principles-based program with demonstrations, exercises, and missions. Subjects include offering value, clear communication, authenticity, and learning from experience.
programs.expandedCopy: This is a candidate for the practice-oriented part of your archive journey. Compare the principles with the recorded examples actually included, then use your own reflection to identify questions for the success call. Recorded accountability material is historical; it does not promise new calls with Julien.
programs.audienceFit: Customers who want a structure for examining application.
programs.publicNotes: Verify recording manifest before release.

programs.title: Transformation Mastery
programs.cardHeadline: Revisit the later framework with more context.
programs.shortCopy: Transformation Mastery's historical structure uses Awareness, Proof, and Permanence, with discussion of scarcity, abundance, emotional patterns, and letting go. It is the later personal-growth chapter many returning customers will recognize.
programs.expandedCopy: Use the earlier archive as a comparison, not a reason to discard what already helped you. The original narrative included dissatisfaction with outward success, so this collection should encourage thoughtful contrast rather than promise that more dates or status will complete your life. Check your existing entitlement before buying another copy.
programs.audienceFit: Customers who want to compare earlier and later approaches.
programs.cta: VIEW TRANSFORMATION MASTERY IN THE ARCHIVE
programs.publicNotes: Removed from the site by owner (2026-10-01).

programs.title: The Jeffy Show
programs.historicalNote: Identified as a recorded RSD program by April 2007 (R01).
programs.cardHeadline: What happens when you stop trying to sound like everyone else?
programs.shortCopy: The Jeffy Show captured a distinctive voice in early RSD, from an era when personality itself became part of the lesson. It adds another perspective to the archive, not another version of anyone else's teaching.
programs.expandedCopy: A useful archive does not require every instructor to sound alike. Compare the style of this program with the others and notice which explanations help you think more clearly about your own communication. It is a historical presentation, not a current mentoring arrangement.
programs.audienceFit: Customers exploring instructor differences.

programs.title: The Resonator
programs.cardHeadline: People don't only hear your words. They hear how you say them.
programs.shortCopy: Explore voice, projection, storytelling, and humor: the delivery layer underneath what you say. Resonator brings a communication-specific focus to the archive, with exercises and examples depending on the edition.
programs.expandedCopy: Confidence is not only a subject to read about; it also affects how a conversation sounds. Study the program's treatment of delivery and expression, then use your coach conversation to choose an appropriate practice focus. Old memberships, free immersion days, and instructor calls are not revived by purchasing the recordings.
programs.audienceFit: Customers interested in spoken communication.
programs.publicNotes: Do not reuse the historical nonverbal-percentage claim.

programs.title: Execute the Program
programs.cardHeadline: Your profile speaks before you do.
programs.shortCopy: Explore how this earlier RSD program approached profiles, photos, messaging, and moving a digital conversation into the real world. Apps and expectations have changed, so study the principles rather than copying old platform instructions.
programs.expandedCopy: Examine the historical approach to presenting yourself and communicating online, while recognizing that apps, features, and expectations have changed. Use principles thoughtfully rather than copying old platform instructions or assuming old example messages suit every person.
programs.audienceFit: Customers studying the online-dating branch of the archive.
programs.publicNotes: Title per owner's comprehensive list (2026-10-01): Execute The Program, 61 lessons.

programs.title: Flawless Natural
programs.cardHeadline: Explore the natural-style branch of RSD.
programs.shortCopy: Flawless Natural is associated with Tim's emphasis on a more natural social style. It offers another perspective for customers comparing structured techniques with personal expression.
programs.expandedCopy: For your archive journey, consider the difference between understanding a framework and sounding rehearsed. Study this historical approach alongside the more systematic programs, then make your own judgment about the ideas that fit.
verifiedThemes: Attitude and expression (subject to manifest review)
programs.audienceFit: Customers who want contrasting teaching approaches.
programs.publicNotes: Removed from the site by owner (2026-10-01).

programs.title: No Reason You're Not Enough (NRYNE)
programs.historicalNote: Identified on the instructor's own site as a 2016 program (R13).
programs.cardHeadline: Compare inner-game teaching across instructors.
programs.shortCopy: Alex's own site identifies NRYNE as an inner-game and personal-development program. It gives returning personal-growth customers another instructor's perspective to examine.
programs.expandedCopy: This is a natural comparison point for someone arriving from a later transformation course. The value is not another promise that you need fixing; it is the opportunity to compare how instructors discussed the internal side of social development. Exact modules should come from the supplied course edition, not the product name.
programs.audienceFit: Customers exploring the internal side of the archive.
programs.publicNotes: Removed from the site by owner (2026-10-01).

programs.title: Social Encrypted
programs.historicalNote: Identified on the instructor's own site as a 2015 program (R13).
programs.cardHeadline: Study the nighttime social setting.
programs.shortCopy: Alex's description identifies Social Encrypted as training about nighttime social events, including instructional video and demonstrated teaching. It complements programs focused on inner work or online interaction.
programs.expandedCopy: Examine how an instructor presented social learning in a particular environment. Compare that context with daytime, social-circle, and online approaches elsewhere in the library. Historical settings and examples are not instructions to ignore current boundaries or assume a venue or person will respond the same way.
programs.audienceFit: Customers comparing different social environments.
programs.publicNotes: Removed from the site by owner (2026-10-01).

programs.title: Evolutions
programs.cardHeadline: Find the stage you are actually studying.
programs.shortCopy: Historical Evolutions material organizes instruction around beginner, intermediate, and advanced perspectives and a sequence of mindset, approach, conversation, and closing stages.
programs.expandedCopy: Use the progression as an object of study, not a claim that every social interaction follows a mechanical formula. It can help you compare different stages of instruction and identify where your own questions belong. The archive edition determines which sections are included.
programs.audienceFit: Customers who appreciate a structured progression.
programs.publicNotes: Removed from the site by owner (2026-10-01).

programs.title: Lifestyle Academy
programs.cardHeadline: Look beyond a single conversation.
programs.shortCopy: Lifestyle Academy's historical positioning extends across values, dating, career, finances, health, and personal direction. It represents a broader lifestyle branch of the archive.
programs.expandedCopy: This is a comparison point for a customer whose interest extends beyond dating techniques. Study how this instructor connected different areas of life, while treating the material as historical self-development education rather than professional financial, medical, or psychological advice. Confirm the exact edition before promising a particular curriculum.
programs.audienceFit: Customers seeking broader context around social development.
programs.publicNotes: Removed from the site by owner (2026-10-01).

programs.title: Ten Commandments of Game
programs.cardHeadline: Examine the principles beneath the tactics.
programs.shortCopy: The historical product centers on ten principles, with supporting lessons and other material depending on the edition. Its positioning emphasizes a foundation beneath individual techniques.
programs.expandedCopy: Use the principle-led structure to compare Derek's approach with other instructors in the archive. Ask which ideas are relevant to your goals and what evidence or practical experience would help you assess them. Old raffles, calls, and immersion offers are not included.
programs.audienceFit: Customers who prefer a clear conceptual structure.
programs.publicNotes: Removed from the site by owner (2026-10-01).

programs.title: Social Circle Blueprint
programs.cardHeadline: Stop chasing individual interactions. Build a life people want to be part of.
programs.shortCopy: Explore the RSD approach to social circles, venues, lifestyle, and the relationships around your social life, rather than isolated introductions.
programs.expandedCopy: For someone familiar with personal-growth work, this collection offers a context to examine how social environments and repeated connections fit alongside individual confidence. Compare its group-oriented approach with the archive's one-to-one and online material. Historical party invitations or live immersion days are not part of the new digital release.
programs.audienceFit: Customers interested in relationships beyond one interaction.
programs.publicNotes: Original edition. Old third-party bonuses excluded.

programs.title: BOSS (The Boss)
programs.cardHeadline: Don't just walk into the room. Learn how to bring something to it.
programs.shortCopy: Conversation. Presence. Body language. Personality. Presentation. Social intelligence. BOSS gives you a window into Madison's approach to becoming a more compelling, expressive, and socially confident man.
programs.expandedCopy: Study how Madison approached interaction, body language, social presence, and personality, then use those lessons to identify where your own charisma can become stronger.
programs.audienceFit: Anyone who wants to become a more engaging communicator without pretending to be somebody else.
programs.publicNotes: Not interchangeable with Get Your Ten or Bootcamp at Home.
programs.themeSourceNote: Conversation/body language/presence/presentation themes come from secondary historical descriptions (R18 and owner-cited Pimp My Mind listing); verify against the edition files.

helpsWith.title: More engaging conversations
helpsWith.text: Understand elements that can help turn surface-level small talk into more engaging interaction.

helpsWith.title: Stronger social presence
helpsWith.text: Study how body language, expression, and engagement influence how you show up around other people.

helpsWith.title: More personality, less performance
helpsWith.text: Instead of hiding behind memorized techniques, examine ways of bringing more of your actual personality into an interaction.

helpsWith.title: Better first impressions
helpsWith.text: Become more conscious of presentation, body language, energy, and communication.

helpsWith.title: Greater social awareness
helpsWith.text: Examine what is happening beyond the words being spoken.

helpsWith.title: More practical charisma
helpsWith.text: Break the vague concept of "being charismatic" into areas you can actually observe and practice.

programs.closingLine: You don't need Madison's personality. You need to discover the most charismatic version of your own.

programs.expandedCopy: Treat this as the instructor's conceptual framework, not established medical science. Compare its language with other programs and use your own judgment. The product page identifies which historical levels and recordings are included; new coaching or treatment is not implied.
programs.audienceFit: Customers who want to compare personal-development perspectives.

programs.title: Daygame by Todd
programs.cardHeadline: What happens when there's no nightclub to hide behind?
programs.shortCopy: No dark room. No loud music. Just you, another person, and your ability to communicate. Daygame by Todd is a historical daytime program in a different setting from the archive's nightlife material.
programs.expandedCopy: Study the instructor's approach in its original context, then compare it with other environments in the collection. Current RSD practice respects whether another person welcomes a conversation and never frames persistence after refusal as a skill to master.
programs.audienceFit: Customers comparing social settings.
programs.cta: TAKE IT INTO THE REAL WORLD
